improper-integral.def: An integral with an infinite limit of integration, such as $\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^2}\,dx$, or with an integrand unbounded on the interval, such as $\int_0^1 \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx$. It is defined as a limit of definite integrals: $\int_a^\infty f(x)\,dx = \lim_{b \to \infty} \int_a^b f(x)\,dx$.

convergence.def: An improper integral converges when the limit of the definite integrals that defines it is a finite number; that number is its value. It diverges when the limit is infinite or does not exist. Example: $\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^2}\,dx$ converges to 1; $\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x}\,dx$ diverges.
